question: What public scheduler/config contract should OpenClaw use for target-specific subagent concurrency limits?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding this capability creates new public config and scheduler semantics that must coordinate with adjacent lane and concurrency proposals.

options.title: Use agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent
options.body: Add the cap under the existing per-agent subagent namespace and keep agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent as the aggregate safety limit.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Scheduler Design
options.body: Defer this issue until caller-selected subagent lanes and foreground per-agent lanes share one coordinated scheduler API.

options.title: Decline New Config Surface
options.body: Keep only the global subagent cap and document local-model serialization workarounds, accepting that target-specific throttling remains unavailable.

recommendation.title: Use agents.list[].subagents.maxConcurrent
recommendation.body: Add the cap under the existing per-agent subagent namespace and keep agents.defaults.subagents.maxConcurrent as the aggregate safety limit.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail runs through the concurrency resolver and gateway lane setup that define this public scheduler/config direction.
